# Build — from an issue to a PR standing at the gate

**Nature: Transmuter** for machinery, **Conjurer** for canon/governance, **Enhancer** for product
code; the mode is named at § 2, and said aloud when it switches mid-run.

> **Give me an issue; I execute the canonical Hatsu protocol (`ren` → `aka` → `mukai` → `en` →
> `third-hand`) and deliver a PR that is `CON-32`-Ready at its human gate — or a G5 stop
> saying exactly why it could not get there.**

**Hatsu holds no CI plane to route work to**, and follows no legacy bankai-core CI capabilities
(no CI agent routing, no CI stage labels, no wave coordinators, no CI wake ladders). Instead,
building an issue is a direct local-plane execution of the canonical Hatsu feature pipeline: author
and locally verify ([`/ren`](../ren/SKILL.md)), publish branch ([`/aka`](../aka/SKILL.md)),
run pre-PR review, tests, coverage, and open PR ([`/mukai`](../mukai/SKILL.md)), observe and
drive PR to readiness ([`/en`](../en/SKILL.md)), and harvest friction after En completes
([`/third-hand`](../third-hand/SKILL.md)).

**The phases this composite calls skip their own `## 0.`**
([`docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md`](../../../../docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md) § 4); the plugin root is
[`docs/PROCESS.md`](../../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Authority every phase shares*.

## 1. Invocation

**P1 — this run opens with `/ten build`** ([`ten`](../ten/SKILL.md) § 6 catches up this phase's
missing prerequisites under its own name; the phases this run calls skip theirs).

```
/build <product|repo_code>#<issue_number>
nen parse build --grammar "<code>#<n>" --line "<the raw invocation>"
nen repo resolve <CODE> --repo <the target repo's own checkout>
```

Case-insensitive; **a code is resolved, never guessed**. A missing argument or configuration item is
asked for and set up inline (`missing-argument`, `missing-configuration`;
[`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § 4 *Ask, set up, continue*): `nen parse` exit `2` or an
unresolved code is the trigger, registered codes the options, absent entry set up in `nen/repos.json`.

**If `#<N>` is already a PR**, do not re-author: hand straight to
[`/en on <CODE>#<N>`](../en/SKILL.md) to drive it to readiness, and say so. Inspect `#<N>` via
`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<N> --jq '.pull_request'`; if populated, it is a PR.

**Say the run started**: it holds a bounded `CON-25` delegation (§ 5), and an unannounced delegation
is one nobody can end.

## 2. Inspect the issue and confirm the mode

Read the target issue before touching code:

```bash
gh issue view <N> --repo <owner/name> --json title,body,state,labels
```

- **If closed**: the run ends immediately, reporting what closed it and which PR delivered it.
- **If an epic awaiting approval**: stop at **G1** (row `mode-label`) — the mode label is the
  maintainer's decision (`CON-4`), never an agent's.
- **Read requirements**: extract issue title, body, acceptance criteria, and technical constraints.

**Confirm Kurapika's work-mode** from the domain and nature of the issue:

| Issue domain / content | Mode |
|---|---|
| Product code implementation, UX, customer-facing behaviour | **Enhancer** |
| Canon prose, governance, constitution (`CON-{n}`), specifications, schemas | **Conjurer** |
| Machinery, tooling, plugin, workflows, scripts, automation | **Transmuter** |

**With ambiguity, propose one and ask** — a wrong mode makes a plausible, wrongly shaped PR: a
**`DECIDE`** per [`jutaisho`](../jutaisho/SKILL.md) § 4, row `mode-unknown`, once per run. A G1
stop is never a mode question: for an unapproved epic the ask is the mode *label*, and **only the
maintainer applies it** (`CON-4`).

## 3. Worktree isolation by default

All authoring, feature work, and verification for the issue **must run in an isolated git worktree**
([`docs/WORKFLOW.md`](../../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § *Where worktrees live*):

```
<core>/.nen/worktrees/<surface>/<name>
```

- Lives git-ignored inside the core checkout, never as a sibling.
- Branch template: `{model}/{persona}/{descriptor}` (from `nen/workflow.json`).
- Core checkout remains clean and parked on trunk (`main`) by default to preserve IDE stability.
- The sole exception is when the maintainer explicitly instructs in prose to work directly on core.

## 4. The canonical feature building protocol

Build drives the issue through the five phases of the canonical Hatsu feature delivery pipeline:
`ren` → `aka` → `mukai` → `en` → `third-hand`.

### Phase 1: `ren` — Author and locally verify

Run [`/ren`](../ren/SKILL.md) to author and locally verify changes addressing the issue:

1. **`breath`**: Warm checkout once per effort, fast-forward base, cut feature branch, prove declared
   iteration checks pass on the clean base tip.
2. **`rasengan`**: Author code changes and focused tests for the issue's acceptance criteria, using
   declared iteration checks and scoped test lane for feedback.
3. **`kokusen`**: Mandatory local checkpoint — verify finished tree with declared iteration checks
   and scoped test lanes, perform staging triage (rejecting scratch/patch/reject files), commit locally
   with multi-line Conventional Commits body and `Hatsu-Agent: Kurapika` trailer.
4. **`amaterasu`**: Launch app where target is declared (or report command if in a worktree).
5. **`spiritual-message`**: Render turn report artifact (`spiritual-message.md`).
6. **`jutaisho`**: Ring turn bell (rung 1).

Repeat `ren` turns until all acceptance criteria are met and committed locally.

### Phase 2: `aka` — Send the branch out

Run [`/aka`](../aka/SKILL.md) to publish the branch to remote:

- Run `gyo` (lint) before rewriting history.
- Squash unpushed commits (never touching published commits).
- Catch up with base (`ao`), re-running `gyo` if catch-up moved the tree.
- Push branch to origin. Opens no pull request.

### Phase 3: `mukai` — Pre-PR verification, review, and open PR

Run [`/mukai`](../mukai/SKILL.md) to execute the pre-PR verification composite and open PR:

1. **Catch-up**: Bring branch up to date with base if needed ([`murasaki`](../murasaki/SKILL.md)).
2. **Adversarial review**: Pre-PR review ([`hanten`](../hanten/SKILL.md)) across raised scopes
   (code practices, architecture, security, performance), settling all findings before proceeding.
3. **Checkpoint**: Local verification checkpoint ([`kokusen`](../kokusen/SKILL.md)).
4. **Impacted tests**: Run impacted unit, UI, and integration suites ([`kotoamatsukami`](../kotoamatsukami/SKILL.md)).
5. **Coverage**: Capture instrumented coverage and measure against threshold ([`byakugan`](../byakugan/SKILL.md)).
6. **PR body and opening**: Compose 9-part PR body from `templates/pr-body.md` with UZF-26 evidence table,
   completion checklist linking issue (`Closes #<N>`), attribution ledger, validate with `nen pr body-check`
   and `pr_body_evidence_check.sh`, open PR ([`shibari`](../shibari/SKILL.md)).
7. **Landing report**: Render landing report artifact (`spiritual-message as landing`).
8. **Handover**: Offer or automatically start [`/en`](../en/SKILL.md) under `mukai.autoEn`.

### Phase 4: `en` — The readiness watch circle

Run [`/en on <CODE>#<PR>`](../en/SKILL.md) to drive PR to verified readiness:

- Hold observation circle under mandatory acting-cycle cap (`monitor.maxCycles`).
- Observe current-head CI checks and reviewer feedback.
- Drive remediation via [`sharingan`](../sharingan/SKILL.md) and catch-up via [`murasaki`](../murasaki/SKILL.md).
- Verify formal readiness: `nen pr ready` must exit 0, verdict quoted verbatim.
- Ring bell at Ready ([`jutaisho`](../jutaisho/SKILL.md)).
- Present PR at its human gate (**G2** delivery, **G4** canon/governance) for maintainer merge decision.

### Phase 5: `third-hand` — Post-En session harvest

Run [`/third-hand`](../third-hand/SKILL.md) to harvest process friction:

- Runs after En completes and stands ready at the gate.
- Raise Netero (`third-hand · netero · <model alias>`) to read sitting transcript.
- Propose 0–3 folded issues through surface picker.
- File only what maintainer chooses with [`file`](../file/SKILL.md), then close session.

## 5. Authority — what this run may and may not do

`CON-25`'s fourth carve-out: holds run-scoped delegation bounded to the pipeline phases.

| | |
|---|---|
| **May execute** | canonical pipeline (`ren` → `aka` → `mukai` → `en` → `third-hand`) for target issue |
| **May author & commit** | in isolated worktree with Conventional Commits and `Hatsu-Agent: Kurapika` |
| **May publish & open PR** | via `aka` and `mukai` using compliant `shibari` template linking the issue |
| **May drive to readiness** | via `en` until `nen pr ready` exits 0 |
| **No CI plane** | holds no CI plane: no CI builder wakes, stage routing, or wave coordinator algorithms |
| **Never** | merges PR (G2/G4 stays maintainer's), applies G1 mode label, votes on reviews, or works on core |

**The delegation expires when the run ends. Say when it ends.**

## 6. When it will not move (G5)

A stall is reported plainly in-session — the blocker, and whether it needs the maintainer:

- Technical blocker or capability gap structurally unresolvable locally is a **G5** naming the gap.
- Render stop banner via `nen stop`, brief decision, letter options with star on recommendation
  per [`jutaisho`](../jutaisho/SKILL.md) § 4.
- Filing is a legitimate outcome: a real defect or missing capability elsewhere is filed with
  [`file`](../file/SKILL.md), linked, and the build held on it.

## 7. Reporting

Every turn that renders a report writes its native artifact before yielding
([`docs/PROCESS.md`](../../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Reporting a phase*):
- `spiritual-message.md` for `ren` turn reports and `mukai` landing reports.
- `rikugan.md` for final delivery state upon completion of `en`.
- Gate determinations require quoting `nen pr ready`'s verdict verbatim.

| Gate | When | The ask |
|---|---|---|
| **G1** | epic awaits mode label (row `mode-label`) | `DECIDE`, with trade-off |
| **G2/G4** | delivery PR is `CON-32`-Ready (rows `merge`, `canon-merge`) | `MERGE`, verdict saying everything |
| **G5** | stuck build or capability gap | `DECIDE`/`DO` with proposed issue; tool per `missing-tool` |

Run **ends** when delivery PR stands Ready at human gate, issue is closed, or at G5 stop: say which,
and that delegation lapsed.

## 8. Resuming & Residue

[`docs/PROCESS.md`](../../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Resuming a run*; each phase is idempotent, and worktree/branch
state records progress. Mode reasoning and G5 diagnosis remain agent judgment. Repos with no `project`
block build with documented commands. PR-vs-issue check stays `gh api` read until dedicated verb.

## 9. Hard limits

- **Never merges a pull request** (`CON-5`/`CON-7`, rows `merge`/`canon-merge`); G2/G4 remain maintainer's gate.
- **Never applies a G1 mode label** on an epic.
- **Never votes, self-reviews, impersonates a reviewer, or casts `request_changes`** (`CON-26`).
- **Never claims a CI builder is doing the work** or uses retired CI capabilities from bankai-core.
- **Never authors, branches, or commits directly on core checkout** by default (Rule 6).
- **Never uses raw `gh pr create`** or skips Mukai's composite steps (pre-PR review, tests, coverage, Shibari body).
- **Never commits without Conventional Commits body and `Hatsu-Agent: Kurapika` trailer**.
- **Never leaves delegation open** — say when it ends.
